title: restore_form_token omits the taken_over_at guard its paired remint_form_token enforces
evidence:
restore_form_token.sql:
UPDATE reference_call
SET form_token = $2::text,
    form_token_expires_at = NULLIF($3, '')::timestamptz
WHERE form_token = $1
  AND status = 'contact_initiated'
RETURNING id::text;

remint_form_token.sql:
WHERE form_token = $1
  AND status = 'contact_initiated'
  AND taken_over_at IS NULL
  AND form_token_expires_at IS NOT NULL
  AND form_token_expires_at < now()
detail: The paired resend queries disagree on taken-over rows: remint refuses them ("a taken-over row's messages are the landlord's domain, A7") but restore does not, so the rollback can resurrect an expired token on a row taken over mid-resend, contradicting save_draft_answer's "the form link stays live through warm handoff" handling in the same chunk.
recommended_fix: Add `AND taken_over_at IS NULL` to restore_form_token's WHERE to mirror remint_form_token's guard, or document explicitly why the rollback may rewrite a taken-over row's token.

title: stamp_form_opened writes with no status/expiry guard despite its 'first live-form GET' docstring
evidence:
stamp_form_opened.sql:
UPDATE reference_call
SET form_opened_at = now()
WHERE form_token = $1
  AND form_opened_at IS NULL
RETURNING id::text;

save_draft_answer.sql (same chunk, for contrast):
AND status = 'contact_initiated'
AND (form_token_expires_at IS NULL OR form_token_expires_at > now())
detail: Docstring promises "the first live-form GET stamps" and the handler treats 0 rows as success, so an expired- or taken-over-page open consumes the one-time stamp; after a later remint the fresh open cannot restamp (IS NULL guard), so completion_seconds spans the dead period.
recommended_fix: Mirror save_draft_answer's live-row guards (status = 'contact_initiated' AND expiry NULL-or-future) in stamp_form_opened, or gate the call in the handler so only live-form GETs stamp.
